card.name: Is/are after a drug name, before property
card.fires_on: The verb "is" or "are" right after a drug name used as the subject, where the next word states a property such as dialyzable, protein bound, or mutagenic. Seen mostly in overdosage and toxicology sections.

modes.label: Dialysis statements
modes.description: "is" or "are" after a drug and its metabolite in overdosage text, ahead of dialyzable or removed by hemodialysis.
modes.example: Cyclophosphamide and its metabolites<< are>> dialyzable.

modes.label: Drug property statements
modes.description: "is" after a drug name in warnings or toxicology text, ahead of an adjective such as mutagenic, immunosuppressive, or protein bound.
modes.example: Mercaptopurine<< is>> immunosuppressive and may impair the

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward a descriptive property term, though the promoted tokens are mostly unrelated fragments.
card.plain: It fires on "is" or "are" right after a drug name, just before the label says what the drug does or whether dialysis clears it.
